intro.text: The yoki-hijo of Torio, taken from her parents as a baby because she was born under a falling star, and raised her whole life for the role.
A yoki-hijo from Torio who escaped the prison the father machine had built for her and freed the hijo from its grasp.

items.text: Yumi was born under a falling star, seen as a sign that she would have a yoki-hijo's powers. She was taken from her parents and raised in the role all her life, becoming famous for her abilities.

The father machine had been activated to replace the yoki-hijo, but it consumed the souls of nearly everyone on the planet; Yumi was among the few survivors. The machine hid her in a simulation of her old life inside the shroud, erasing each day's memories, for 1,763 years, until her ritual summoned thirty-seven hijo at once and pulled one spirit free of the machine. She then passed out from exhaustion.
The freed spirit begged Yumi for help, then followed Liyun into Kilahito as a nightmare, found Painter and Connected him to Yumi to protect her memories. This unintentionally made them switch bodies.

Painter appeared in Yumi's form, though Yumi alone saw him as himself. His disregard for every ritual left her stressed and humiliated; believing the spirits were punishing her, she finally exploded at him. Painter explained he was a real person, and Yumi decided the spirits had sent him to help her save them.

In Painter's body, Yumi's strong Investiture quickly reshaped it to match her own. She did not realize this until Foreman Sukishi came to the door and was shocked to find a woman in Painter's room. Following Painter's instructions, she told the foreman he was ill and told him about the stable nightmare.

Yumi met Akane, who knew Painter, and was struck by her beauty. At Painter's urging she lied that she was his sister. When Akane mistook her for one of Painter's concubines, Yumi corrected her, then realized Painter had been lying to her. When he admitted it, she had a panic attack.

Yumi calmed herself by stacking books, eating and discovering television, then fell asleep and woke back in her own place. When Liyun confronted Painter about the day before, Yumi had him repeat her exact words; Liyun believed them, and they went on to the kimomakkin.

Despite their bad start, Yumi and Akane soon became good friends, though Akane believed Yumi was Painter's sister from another city. Akane helped Yumi feel freer to be herself and express her feelings.

Yumi's attendant Hwanji, once an attendant to the retired yoki-hijo Dwookim, liked to hum while caring for her. When Painter, in Yumi's place, grew rebellious, Hwanji feared Liyun would blame her, but Yumi promised to say it wasn't her fault. Hwanji told Yumi about the reform movement.

Yumi had always cared for her attendants, including Chaeyung, who could comb out her hair's tangles painlessly, but her station kept her from really talking with them. Once she began speaking with them more, she found Chaeyung and Hwanji eager to talk with her.

Yumi learned that Liyun, who had effectively raised her, had kept her in the dark all her life. She felt betrayed and frustrated yet still respected Liyun, and was deeply hurt by the disappointed, aggressive way Liyun responded when confronted.
In the end, Yumi escaped her prison and freed the hijo from the father machine.

personality.text: Yumi is unhappy with her life and wishes for something more, but forces herself to accept it and its rules without question. When she starts to wonder whether she could do more with her life, she hates herself for the thought.
Yumi hates lies, having been taught all her life that they are evil, and judges harshly anyone who tells them.
Yumi is modest, preferring clothes that hide her figure and cover her skin, though she relaxes this as she lets herself be more expressive.
As yoki-hijo, Yumi summons the hijo through ritual stone stacking and can have them take the shape of tools to help the people of Torio. She is very heavily Invested.
Yumi tends to stack nearby objects when stressed or anxious, and sometimes simply for fun. Raised speaking the Torio language, she has an accent that sounds strange to the people of Nagadan.
